name: The Specials
hook: A deliberately mixed-race Coventry band that fused ska and punk, ran its own label, and took a song about empty, riot-hit cities to number one.
blurb: The Specials formed in Coventry in 1977, started by Jerry Dammers, who has said he built the band on purpose to bring Black and white musicians together. They mixed Jamaican ska with the energy of punk. In 1978 Joe Strummer invited them on the Clash's 'On Parole' tour, which gave them their first national attention, and they briefly shared the Clash's management. Dammers started his own label, 2 Tone, and their first single, 'Gangsters' (1979), was built on Prince Buster's 'Al Capone'. Their first album was produced by Elvis Costello. In 1981 'Ghost Town', about cities hit by unemployment, went to number one during the recession and a summer of riots in British cities. The classic line-up split that year when Terry Hall, Neville Staple and Lynval Golding left to form Fun Boy Three.
